newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Most basis offers stay flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Most basis offers stay flat.

text.p: Most soymeal basis offers remained flat in response to lackluster demand in domestic and export markets, U.S. cash soymeal brokers said Thursday.
"Meal basis is very disappointing," said an Indiana dealer. "The people on the river are really hitting the domestic market because there's no export business right now."
Most in the trade had expected a sharp reduction in last week's crushing pace to reduce available soymeal supplies and support the basis.
But most basis levels this week have remained unchanged.
Cash sources are divided over whether this week's soybean crush will be higher or lower than last week's pace of 25.938 million bushels.
Estimates for this week's National Oilseed Processor Association's crush ranged from 25.5 to 26.5 million bushels.
Weekly soymeal export sales data from USDA came in well above expectations and was considered supportive to the markets.
USDA reported sales of 139,400 tonnes. That figure compares with trade expectations for 40,000 to 60,000 tonnes.
